answer: The network keeps an atlas charting work as territory on a shared ocean; payout weight equals mapped area times depth. Each verified epoch plants a ferrous anchor - an iron-clad proof bound to that epoch's beacon, unmovable, uncopyable. A fleet's clones chart the same shallow coastline, since identical behavior maps to identical coordinates, so the atlas exposes them as one landmass: splitting across n clones divides the same area instead of multiplying it. Forging deep territory for n clones requires n times the real voyages. One honest agent charts new ground.
